newsitem.title: USA: Congressional panels to urge independent counsel.
newsitem.headline: Congressional panels to urge independent counsel.

text.p: Members of the House and Senate judiciary committees will urge Attorney General Janet Reno to take action that could lead to an independent counsel to investigate campaign funding abuses, congressional officials said on Thursday.

A spokesman for House Judiciary Committee Chairman Henry Hyde, an Illinois Republican, said committee Republicans were sending a letter to Reno asking her to seek an independent counsel. A similar letter was being circulated among Senate Judiciary Committee members, sources said.

Once enough signatures are obtained, the Senate letter will be sent to Reno asking her to start the procedure that could lead to an outside special prosecutor to investigate financing practices that have ensnarled President Bill Clinton and Democrats in controversy.
Neither committee would release the contents of the letters.
Officials in the House and Senate said Democrats, who are in a minority in Congress, would be asked to sign the letters but it was not certain how many, if any, would do so.

Republicans, and several Democrats as well, have urged Reno independently to take action to appoint a special prosecutor to investigate widespread reports of irregularities -- nearly all of them involving improper, illegal or questionable donations to Democrats for the 1996 campaign.

She has turned down the requests so far, saying there is no "specific, credible evidence" of a crime that would specifically trigger an independent probe. She has also argued that any wrongdoing could be investigated by a Justice Department task force that now includes 31 FBI agents.

Under the independent counsel law, a majority of either Republican or Democratic members of the House or Senate judiciary committees can ask the attorney general to start the process toward naming an independent counsel.

Once Reno gets the letter or letters from the judiciary committees seeking an independent counsel, she must submit a report within 30 days on whether a preliminary investigation has or will begin on the matter and give her reasons why.

If she decides to start a preliminary investigation, Reno has another 90 days to decide if there are "reasonable grounds" to believe there should be a further investigation by an independent counsel. If she concludes there are reasonable grounds, she can apply to a special three-judge federal panel that would appoint an outside counsel.
